passage: "Rafiq, the invoices are missing again," I whispered at six, and then fixed it myself before our director's review, saying nothing. The first time, two months back, that felt like kindness. By the third time I noticed Rafiq had stopped double-checking anything, because I always would. That evening I saw that my cover was costing Rafiq the chance to learn, and it was making me a little dishonest with our director. So the next morning I asked Rafiq for ten minutes, laid out the three misses, and we built a checklist together. Then I told the director myself: there had been slips, Rafiq was owning them, and here was the fix. My heart was pounding. The director only asked to see the checklist. Jahnavi

qa.q: What was missing before the director's review?
Why was Jahnavi's heart pounding when talking to the director?
qa.a: Jahnavi was nervous about admitting the earlier slips openly after keeping quiet, yet chose honesty anyway.

qa.q: What could Jahnavi do if Rafiq slips again?
qa.a: Point it out kindly, ask Rafiq to fix it and to tell the director, using the shared checklist.

qa.q: How might Rafiq have felt when Jahnavi laid out the three misses?
qa.a: Rafiq may have felt embarrassed to learn the covering had been noticed, but also glad to get a fair chance to learn.

grounding: The narrator has been covering a junior's mistakes, sees it blocks learning, and coaches the junior while staying honest with the director.
